motor.description: Motor dysgraphia involves difficulties with fine motor control affecting handwriting quality
keyIndicators: High Mean Squared Error (MSE) in drawing tasks
Slow writing speed with poor legibility
motor.research: Rosenblum et al. (2020) found MSE >38 in children aged 7-9 correlated with motor dysgraphia diagnosis at 78% accuracy in a study of 500 children
interventions: Occupational therapy focusing on pencil grip and posture
Handwriting practice with large letters and guided lines
Fine motor activities: clay modeling, bead threading
Assistive technology: pencil grips, slant boards

spatial.description: Spatial dysgraphia involves difficulty organizing letters and words on the page
keyIndicators: Poor spatial planning in drawing tasks
spatial.research: Berninger & Wolf (2009) identified spatial planning deficits in 23% of children with writing difficulties
interventions: Graph paper for initial writing practice
Visual-spatial activities: puzzles, pattern copying
Highlighted baseline and margin markers
Digital writing tools with automatic spacing

phonological.description: Difficulty processing and manipulating speech sounds, affecting reading and spelling
keyIndicators: Increased response time for phonological tasks
Difficulty with rhyming and sound blending
phonological.research: Snowling (2019) meta-analysis of 150 studies confirms phonological deficit is present in 80% of dyslexia cases
interventions: Structured phonics programs (Orton-Gillingham, Wilson)
Multisensory learning: visual, auditory, kinesthetic
Daily 20-minute phonemic awareness practice
Audio books paired with text reading

dyscalculia.description: Specific learning difficulty affecting mathematical abilities and number sense
dyscalculia.research: Butterworth (2005) identified deficient number sense in children with dyscalculia affects 5-7% of school population
interventions: Concrete manipulatives: counting blocks, number lines
Visual math strategies: drawing, graphing
Frequent practice with basic facts using games
Technology: math apps with adaptive difficulty

dyspraxia.description: Developmental Coordination Disorder affecting motor planning and execution
dyspraxia.research: Wilson & McKenzie (2018) found motor planning deficits in 90% of children diagnosed with dyspraxia (n=300)
interventions: Physical therapy focusing on motor planning
Rhythmic activities: drumming, dance, martial arts
Breaking tasks into smaller sequential steps
Visual schedules and movement cues

nvld.description: Nonverbal Learning Disability affecting visual-spatial and social perception
keyIndicators: Strong verbal but weak visual processing
nvld.research: Rourke (1989, updated 2020) identified NVLD affects 1-2% of children, often co-occurring with ADHD
interventions: Explicit teaching of visual-spatial concepts
Memory strategies: chunking, verbal mediation
Social skills training with visual supports
Preferential seating for clear board visibility

normalRanges.description: Normative baseline data for typically developing children

rules.description: Single indicator outside normal range - monitor, not diagnostic
Two corroborating indicators - recommend professional evaluation
Three or more indicators - strong likelihood, urgent evaluation recommended

confidenceCalculation.research: Best practice guidelines (IDA, 2021) recommend multiple assessment points before diagnosis

kerala.educationSystem: High literacy rate (94%), strong emphasis on academic achievement
kerala.commonConcerns: Pressure for performance, stigma around learning difficulties
kerala.supportiveApproach: Emphasize strengths, frame interventions as skill-building
kerala.languageConsiderations: Malayalam script complexity may affect dyslexia presentation
